jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.excerpt: Aetonix is a digital health company building a chronic care management platform for U.
jobs.description:
Aetonix is a digital health company building a chronic care management platform for U.S. health systems, clinics, and ACOs. Our product has two faces:

  • A mobile app that helps Medicare patients (65+) complete simple, guided check ins, and
  • A desktop app that helps care teams know which patients need them most — and act.

We are backed by Trudell Medical International (TMI), a Canadian-headquartered medical device company. We operate with patient capital and startup urgency.

The next 6 months are about proving product-market fit with real clinical evidence in a category where fewer than 4% of eligible U.S. patients are currently receiving the care they are entitled to.

ABOUT THIS ROLE

You'll join our design team – working alongside our Product Designer and Lead Product Designer – as a senior contributor across the patient mobile app and care-team desktop app, owning specific product surfaces end-to-end and raising the craft bar within your area.

You’ll report directly to the VP of Product, and partner closely with the Lead Product Designer on shared design system standards, growing our research practice, and raising the bar on the team’s design craft.

HATS YOU WEAR

Craft Contributor Your work sets the example within your surface area, and raises the bar for the team around you.

  • Deliver high-quality, well-reasoned design from problem framing through shipped product.
  • Give structured critique that builds design taste and judgment in others.
  • Contribute to our evolving design system across web and mobile surfaces.

Researcher You run and synthesize lean research, and share those learnings with peers.

  • Lead qualitative and quantitative research with care teams and Medicare patients.
  • Recognize when data or research is missing and go get it — designing the study, recruiting, and synthesizing findings.
  • Translate complex clinical workflows into clear, intuitive software interactions.

Discovery Partner You bring a user-grounded point of view to the product decisions that shape your surface.

  • Participate in product decisions as a full voice, grounded in user insight.
  • Push back when a problem needs more framing before solutions are explored.
  • Frame recommendations in the language of outcomes and impact.

Communicator You tell a crisp story that connects the design to the people it serves.

  • Confidently present design work to cross functional peers, innovation partners, and executives when needed.
  • Use story maps, journey maps, and similar tools so product, design, and engineering align on risks and priorities.
  • Bring patient and clinician voices into trade off discussions so core perspectives shape final decisions.

MUST HAVE

  • 5–7+ years of experience in product design, with a portfolio showing end-to-end ownership from research through shipped product.
  • Strong research skills: able to run a usability study, synthesize findings quickly, and share what you learn with others.
  • Hands on with AI/ML powered product design. You have experimented with AI or ML features, and can explain what “good” looks like.
  • Experience contributing to and working within a shared design system (web + mobile), in partnership with other designers and engineers.
  • Solid accessibility practice baked into your work (keyboard and screen-reader flows, clear focus states, robust interaction patterns).
  • Familiarity with product analytics tools (e.g., Amplitude) to uncover usage patterns and inform design decisions.
  • Active use of AI design and research tooling (e.g., Claude, Figma Make or equivalents) to accelerate prototyping, synthesis, and research; teaches others to do the same.
  • Ability to craft compelling design stories that win buy-in from engineers and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Comfort giving and receiving structured feedback, with genuine interest in helping other designers grow, even without a formal mentorship mandate.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Background in healthcare, clinical, or regulated software. You understand what HIPAA and clinical workflows mean for design decisions.
  • Behavioral science experience; designing for habit formation, engagement, or behavior change.
  • Familiarity with CCM, RPM, or chronic disease management platforms.
  • AI/ML product design experience in a healthcare or clinical context: conversational interfaces, clinical decision support, or data-heavy dashboards.
  • WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility expertise in a regulated health context.

WHO YOU ARE

  • A builder. Most energized when you are crafting something new, not polishing something established.
  • Mission-driven. You care about patients and want your design work to have measurable impact on how chronic disease is managed.
  • Humble enough to listen deeply to a care coordinator, confident enough to challenge a product decision, and persuasive enough to translate both for executive stakeholders.

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Fully remote: open to candidates in Canada or the United States. EST/CST overlap preferred for core collaboration hours.
  • Occasional in-person team meetings in Ottawa, London (Ontario) and Toronto, Canada areas (travel required on a quarterly basis at minimum).
  • Comprehensive benefits package including health insurance, RSP matching, and professional development opportunities.

WHAT WE OFFER:

  • An agile, dynamic and motivated team working together in a fast-growing company that is changing the future of virtual care
  • The ability to make a real difference in people’s lives
  • Health insurance including medical, dental, vision and life

Aetonix Systems Inc. is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all teammates. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the target for new hire salaries for the advertised position. Within the range, individual compensation is determined by job-related skills and knowledge, relevant professional, lived experience, and/or work location. Our compensation policies and practices are designed to allow our colleagues’ growth and salary progression as they develop in their role. jobs.description:
[We show compassion to heal minds.]

🧠 About Legion Health

Legion Health is a technology-forward psychiatry company delivering world-class outpatient mental health care while expanding access for patients through insurance.

We are seeking exceptional Psychiatrists (MD or DO) across the United States who are passionate about evidence-based psychiatry and want the time, support, and clinical autonomy needed to provide exceptional patient care.

Our innovative model combines the stability of a traditional hospital position with the flexibility of a private practice. We prioritize our clinicians' well-being and professional growth, offering a competitive compensation package and fostering a vibrant, collaborative culture.

Quality and patient experience are paramount to us. This means recruiting exceptional providers, championing evidence-based protocols, and displaying compassion in every patient interaction. Our exceptional psychiatrists operate with clinical autonomy, supported by experienced peers.

Our vision is to pioneer a new era of medicine by delivering world-class psychiatry. We believe in a future where every person can access the compassionate, high-quality care they need.

🚀 About the Role

Practice at the top of your license, from wherever you do your best work. This role is designed for psychiatrists who want meaningful clinical autonomy without having to build and operate a private practice alone.

We are looking for clinically excellent, patient-centered psychiatrists to provide psychiatric care through telehealth. Full-time and part-time positions are available.

💙 Benefits

Legion’s model is built to give clinicians more time for patients, fewer administrative distractions, and the support of a high-caliber psychiatric community.

  • Flexibility: Set your own schedule for optimal work-life balance.

  • Work from Home: See patients from the comfort of your home via telehealth.

  • Significant Administrative Support: You focus on patient care, and we’ll handle scheduling, insurance verification, billing, prior authorizations, pharmacy coordination, etc.

  • Patient Acquisition: Unlike with a private practice, we’ll work to fill your schedule, so you don’t have to do your own marketing.

  • Competitive Pay: We compensate our providers at market-leading rates.

  • Weekly Pay: We pay our providers every week for immediate financial benefit and planning ease.

  • Legal Protection: We provide full malpractice insurance coverage.

  • Clinical Autonomy: We hire the most skilled providers and trust them to do what’s best for patients.

  • Technical Support: We cover the costs for you to have best-in-class EHR, e-Prescribe, and AI tools.

  • Credentialing Support: We handle all aspects and costs of credentialing with a large number of insurance plans, including commercial, ACA, and government, ensuring your legal and effective authorization within insurance networks.

  • Licensure and DEA Coverage: We’ll reimburse you for all fees associated with getting licensed in other states as required by Legion.

  • Commitment to Responsible Prescribing and High-Quality Care: We have rigorous, evidence-based protocols and provide objective diagnostic tools to ensure responsible and ethical prescriptions of controlled substances.

  • Community of Clinical Excellence: You will work alongside the most talented psychiatrists in the world. Our current psychiatrists have trained at some of the country’s most prestigious institutions.

  • Opportunities for Professional Growth: As we expand, we intend to promote clinical leadership from the best of our active providers.

  • Culture of Excellence through Innovation: Actively participate in ushering in a new era of mental health care through superior clinical care and technology.

  • Resources: We provide premium subscriptions to resources such as UpToDate and Carlat.

  • Exclusive Events: Engage with your colleagues through exclusive in-person and virtual events.

✅ Responsibilities

  • Provide excellent patient care for conditions including depression, anxiety, ADHD, insomnia, PTSD, bipolar disorder, etc.

  • Perform comprehensive psychiatric assessments, including mental-health history, medical history, diagnostic evaluation, and risk analysis.

  • Create and execute individualized treatment plans that may combine medication management and brief psychotherapy.

  • Provide compassionate, respectful, and patient-centered care.

  • Use evidence-based clinical protocols and responsible prescribing practices.

  • Collaborate with other psychiatrists through consultations and case reviews.

  • Use technology and operational systems effectively to deliver reliable telehealth care.

🧰 Qualifications

  • An active, unrestricted license to practice medicine in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

  • Strong clinical assessment, diagnostic, and medication-management skills.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Comfort providing care remotely and using electronic health record systems.

  • Commitment to patient-centered, compassionate, evidence-based care.

📍 Role Logistics

  • Location: Fully remote within the United States.

  • Schedule: Full-time or part-time positions are available.

  • Expected annual compensation: $300K–$500K, depending on completed patient-care hours.

🤝 Clinical Advisory Board

Legion’s Clinical Advisory Board brings together nationally recognized psychiatrists, physician executives, telepsychiatry pioneers, and primary-care leaders. Working closely with Legion’s medical leadership, they help shape our clinical quality standards, evidence-based care protocols, prescribing safeguards, risk-management practices, and continuous quality-improvement efforts as the company scales.

We are looking for a Senior DevOps Engineer to build and scale the continuous integration, testing, and release infrastructure for NVIDIA Isaac Sim!


NVIDIA Isaac Sim is a cutting-edge robotics simulation platform that empowers researchers and engineers to accelerate the development and deployment of intelligent robots. Leveraging the power of NVIDIA's AI and GPU technologies, Isaac Sim offers a realistic and scalable environment for training, validating, and optimizing robots for real-world scenarios.


You will work closely with Isaac Sim developers, QA, and infrastructure teams to make software delivery faster, more reliable, and reproducible. Your work will enable engineers to identify regressions early and deliver high-quality releases across supported platforms.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Design, develop, and operate CI/CD pipelines for building, testing, packaging, and releasing Isaac Sim and its components.
  • Own GPU-enabled CI runners and test environments across on-premises and cloud infrastructure, including provisioning, scheduling, capacity planning, and recovery.

jobs.title: Robotics AI Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About Menlo Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it.
jobs.description:
About Menlo
Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role
As a Robotics AI Engineer, you will work at the intersection of learning and hardware, training and deploying policies that run on Asimov in the real world. This is not a research role in the traditional sense. You will be expected to get results on physical robots, not just in simulation, and to iterate fast when things break. You will work closely with the hardware, firmware, and infrastructure teams to close the loop between training and deployment.

What You Will Do

  • Design and train RL and imitation learning policies for locomotion, manipulation, or whole-body control

  • Run experiments on physical hardware and close the sim-to-real gap through systematic debugging and domain adaptation

  • Build and maintain simulation environments and data pipelines that support fast policy iteration

  • Instrument robot deployments and analyze failure modes to feed improvements back into training

  • Collaborate with hardware and firmware engineers to understand physical constraints and improve policy robustness

What We Are Looking For

  • Strong foundations in reinforcement learning or imitation learning, with hands-on experience training policies that run on real systems

  • Comfort working directly with robots, not just simulators

  • Proficiency in Python and familiarity with standard RL/ML frameworks (JAX, PyTorch, IsaacGym/IsaacLab, MuJoCo, or similar)

  • An empirical, debugging-first mindset, you care about what actually works on hardware

  • Ability to move fast and context-switch between research problems and engineering tasks

Nice to Have

  • Prior work on humanoid or legged robot platforms

  • Experience with sim-to-real transfer techniques (domain randomization, system identification, noise injection)

  • Contributions to open-source robotics projects

  • Background in control theory, trajectory optimization, or dynamics

Why Join Menlo
The policies you train do not sit in a notebook. They run on a real humanoid, in the real world, on short feedback loops. You will see your work move physical hardware within days, not quarters. You will collaborate directly with the hardware, firmware, and infrastructure teams, with high visibility and real stakes, and everything you can open-source, you will. If you want to build the systems that turn software into physical labor, this is where it happens.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.description:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About the team and role:

Mozilla’s mission is to champion the internet as a global public resource, measured through a double bottom line: advancing that mission while succeeding in the market. At the Mozilla Corporation, we live our mission thesis through building our and scaling trusted, user-first products, with a focus on the Firefox browser. The global public policy team enables this by shaping laws and regulatory frameworks that support our open source technologies, strengthen user choice and privacy, and ensure fair competition to create the conditions for responsible innovation and long-term growth. Do you like working on big-picture problems? Join us to influence the future of tech policy!

Mozilla is looking for an experienced Policy Communications Europe Lead to help set the public narrative on the role our browser, Firefox, and browser engine, Gecko, play in order to keep the web open. We build products in the public interest to support the Mozilla project. The work will cover privacy, AI, open source, competition, and internet policy—translating the positions Mozilla’s policy team develops into stories that get ahead of the debate, not just respond to it. In this pivotal role, you’ll drive Mozilla’s proactive policy media voice across regions and audiences, build narratives, craft media relationships, and build credibility amongst key stakeholders.

You’ll translate complex, high-stakes policy issues into stories that connect, inspire, and drive impact. You’ll help Mozilla—and the people and partners who believe in an open internet—cut through noise, frame critical debates, and spotlight what’s at stake for users everywhere.

What you'll do:

As Policy Communications Lead for Europe, you will:

  • Sit in the Policy & Comms organisation, reporting to the Europe Policy Lead.
  • Focus on Europe as your key region, but be able and ready to apply your skills to emerging key markets for Firefox on other continents.
  • Be a central operator, translating policy strategy into public narrative that advances the products we build and the changes they are advocating for on the web.
  • Own and drive Mozilla’s proactive media narrative on privacy, security, AI, open-source, competition, and emerging regulatory issues—translating policy positions into stories that get ahead of the debate rather than following it.
  • Place and amplify a steady cadence of thought leadership pieces such that put Mozilla’s policy positions in front of the right audiences.
  • Serve as a strategic partner and trusted advisor to communications colleagues and senior Mozilla leaders, supporting proactive and reactive policy comms across the organisation.
  • Work cross-functionally with marketing, legal, product and engineering teams to shape narratives that advance Mozilla’s mission and differentiate our voice from “Big Tech.”
  • Build and nurture relationships with key journalists, policymakers, industry, thought leaders, advocacy organizations, and influencers in technology, digital rights, and policy spheres.
  • Craft and edit a wide range of materials—press releases, blog posts, policy statements, op-eds, speeches, regulatory submissions, and executive briefing documents.
  • Prepare Mozilla spokespeople for high-stakes media, public, and policy engagements, including message development, media training, and issue briefing.
  • Track and respond to fast-moving external developments, helping Mozilla seize moments to lead important conversations and manage risks.
  • Help shape Mozilla’s public policy positioning on critical product initiatives, supporting launches, campaigns, and issue-based advocacy.
  • Work closely with the wider communications team and external agency partners to ensure clarity, alignment, and operational rigor across channels.
  • Serve as a point of escalation and counsel in high-risk, complex, or crisis policy scenarios.

What You’ll Bring:

  • 5-10 years of experience in policy communications, media relations, or related roles, ideally in technology, advocacy, or policy-driven environments.
  • Exceptional writing and editing skills—with the ability to distill complexity into clarity, urgency, and actionable narrative.
  • Deep knowledge of technology policy issues such as privacy, data, AI, competition, digital rights, open source, and internet regulation.
  • A track record of building strong relationships with journalists, policymakers, and policy-focused organizations globally.
  • Experience advising and supporting senior executives on high-profile, high-stakes communications and issues management.
  • Strategic instincts, operational rigor, and comfort with ambiguity and rapid change.
  • Confidence operating in a global, remote, and mission-driven organization.
  • Experience supporting product communications and collaborating with engineering/technical teams.
  • Ability to balance strategic vision with hands-on execution—no job is too big or too small.
  • Passion for Mozilla’s mission: making the internet safer, more open, and more human.

Bonus Points For:

  • Experience in both in-house and agency settings.
  • Additional languages beyond English, particularly French and German will be an asset.
  • Prior experience in open-source, civil society, or non-profit tech environments.

What you’ll get:

  • Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team
  • Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute)

About Mozilla

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online.

Job title:Director, Transactional Risk Monitoring

Reports to:SVP, Enterprise Risk

Department:Business Resource Group

Location:Remote (GA, NY, TN - preferred)

Grade:17

About Priority Commerce:

Priority Commerce is a leading financial technology company on a mission to deliver a personalized, easy-to-adopt financial toolset that accelerates cash flow and optimizes working capital for businesses. Our vision is to eliminate the barriers to unlocking revenue - empowering businesses to grow faster and operate smarter.

We achieve this through the Priority Commerce Engine, an innovative platform that combines payables, acquiring, and banking and treasury solutions. This unified approach allows businesses to streamline financial operations, reduce unnecessary costs, and uncover new revenue opportunities.

At Priority Commerce, we're driven by results. We expect our people tobe known for results- bringing expertise, momentum, and relentless focus to every challenge, helping our clients and each other thrive.

About the Role:

We are looking for a Director, Banking, Treasury & Platform Transactional Risk Monitoring to own day-to-day fraud and credit risk monitoring for Priority’s Banking, Treasury & Platform services. Priority Commerce operates on a program manager model — Priority Commerce onboards program managers, who in turn onboard the underlying businesses and/or consumers that actually transact. This role is responsible for monitoring risk at both layers: the program manager level and the underlying accountholder level beneath each program. You'll be the person accountable for catching and resolving risk issues day to day, including with our card issuing programs.

Responsibilities:

  • Own day-to-day fraud and credit risk transaction monitoring for Priority’s Banking and Treasury Platform — alert review, investigation, case disposition, and loss mitigation across account takeover, first-party fraud, synthetic identity, and payment fraud typologies.

  • Monitor risk across all layers of the platform: at the program manager level (overall program-level activity and exposure) and at the underlying business/consumer accountholder level that each program manager onboards.

  • Review and act on daily transaction, account, and case activity to identify emerging fraud rings, loss trends, and credit deterioration signals — driving the alerts to resolution, not just triage.

  • Manage credit risk exposure for accountholders on an ongoing basis — applying underwriting criteria, tracking exposure limits, and executing account review triggers at both the program manager and end-accountholder level.

  • Support Priority’s card issuing programs from a risk and fraud perspective — monitoring card-present and card-not-present activity and managing dispute/chargeback trends.

  • Tune and calibrate existing monitoring rules and scoring models to reduce false positives and minimize fraud/credit losses while preserving a smooth customer experience; recommend enhancements as volume and program manager count scale.

  • Build and maintain fraud and credit loss reporting and dashboards for internal leadership, tracking loss rates, alert volumes, recovery rates, and key risk indicators across program managers and underlying accountholders.

  • Respond to partner bank inquiries related to fraud and credit risk on Priority’s Commerce platform, and provide reporting and updates in line with each bank's requirements.

  • Partner with internal product and engineering teams to close control gaps and inform product decisions that affect fraud or credit exposure.

  • Document day-to-day procedures for the monitoring program and prepare the team to bring on analyst support as alert volume grows.

  • Maintain baseline awareness of BSA/AML and regulatory obligations as they intersect with fraud and credit risk work, partnering with the Compliance team and partner banks on any BSA/AML-specific requirements.

What Success Looks Like:

  • You own the risk results for your product lines, helping your product areas hit overall financial targets.

  • You partner with the business leaders for your products to effectively balance revenue growth, customer friction, and risk.

  • You establish effective and efficient transaction monitoring policies and procedures.

  • You are flexible, working with customers and prospects that have unique needs while also delivering a scalable risk management environment.

  • You maintain effective relationships with banking partners.

Candidate Requirements:

  • 10+ years of experience in banking fraud risk, credit risk, or transaction monitoring, ideally within a bank, fintech, payments company, or embedded banking/BaaS environment.

  • Proven track record owning day-to-day transaction risk monitoring — working alerts and cases to resolution, not just designing the rules that generate them.

  • Experience monitoring risk across a multi-layer program structure (e.g., a program manager, ISO, or platform model where sub-merchants, businesses, or consumers are onboarded beneath an intermediate program) is a strong plus.

  • Track record of reducing fraud or credit losses through rule tuning, model calibration, or policy changes, with the data to back it up.

  • Experience with fraud detection, case management, or credit decisioning systems

  • Experience supporting a card issuing program — familiarity with bank oversight processes and dispute and chargeback procedures.

  • Familiarity with payments and treasury products — ACH, wires, card transactions, embedded banking, or similar — is a strong plus.

  • Comfortable working independently in a fast-moving, high-volume caseload environment.

  • Strong analytical skills and comfort with data — able to spot patterns in transaction and account data and translate them into policy or rule changes.

  • Working knowledge of BSA/AML fundamentals is helpful but not the focus of this role; day-to-day compliance and SAR filing sit with a separate Compliance function.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills; comfortable corresponding with partner banks on routine fraud and credit matters.

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Business, Statistics, or related field, or equivalent experience.

Work Environment & Culture:

We believe that performance and experience go hand in hand -an exceptional employee experience is earned through contribution. We are a results-driven team, grounded in our core values: ownership, authenticity, service, trust, innovation, and camaraderie.

Our culture is built for those who want to make an impact. We challenge each other to grow, celebrate progress, and support one another through shared goals and real connection. Whether you're building technology, serving clients, or supporting internal teams, you’ll be part of a company that empowers you to perform at your best and be known for results.

Compensation and Benefits:

Compensation range:$125k - $150k

We invest in the whole employee - personally and professionally. Our benefits package is designed to support your well-being, growth, and success - both inside and outside of work.

Financial Wellness

  • Bonus programs

  • 401(k) match

  • HSA and FSA options

Time Off

Growth & Development

  • Education expense reimbursement

  • Leadership development programs

  • Certified Payments Professional (CPP) certification support

We believe great performance starts with feeling supported - and we’ve built our benefits with that in mind.

Traditional Physical Requirements:

  • Requires prolonged sitting, standing, bending, stooping and stretching.

  • Requires the ability to lift 10 pounds.

  • Requires eye-hand coordination, manual dexterity and a normal range of hearing and vision (with or without correction).

Join our team at Priority Commerce and be part of a dynamic and innovative company that is transforming the financial technology landscape. Together, we can shape the future of payments and banking solutions while providing unmatched value to our clients.

Data Systems Development & Integration

jobs.description:
About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 102.4 million monthly active users (MAU), as of June 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit .

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above.

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed withI mean or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

Our Services engineering teams, part of our Quality and Scale Pillar, build and run the systems every Life360 member relies on but never sees. We carry location data between members’ phones and our servers, deliver the push and SMS notifications that families depend on, verify who members are and what they can access, build and scale our business critical services and give partners a safe way to build on Life360. When we do our jobs well, product teams ship faster and families trust the app in the moments that matter most.

We are a group of backend, cloud, and mobile engineers who care about reliability, security, and scale, and who treat member trust as the foundation of everything we build.

About the Job

As a Director of Engineering, you will lead the teams building and operating Life360’s critical platforms, including location and messaging, cloud infrastructure and identity, and partner ecosystems. These systems are the foundation of the experiences millions of families rely on every day. You are a player coach who will set technical direction, develop strong engineering managers and technical leaders, and ensure our platforms are reliable, secure, and built to scale as Life360 grows to hundreds of millions of members worldwide.

This is a leadership role that combines deep technical judgment with business impact. You will anticipate scaling challenges before they become problems, modernize critical systems, and make thoughtful tradeoffs across reliability, performance, cost, and speed. You will partner closely with Product, Security, Data, and engineering leaders to connect technology investments to business outcomes, accelerate product innovation, and build an engineering organization that can deliver at scale.

For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $216,500 to $318,500 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is 251,000 to 295,000 CAD. Note: Please be aware that the job title for positions in Canada will be "Developer" in lieu of "Engineer." We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers.

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits.

What You’ll Do

  • Build the foundation for scale. Lead the engineering teams behind Life360’s critical services, including location and messaging, cloud and identity, and partner platforms. Build reliable, secure, and scalable systems that can support hundreds of millions of members around the world.
  • See around corners. Anticipate architectural bottlenecks, reliability risks, and scaling challenges before they impact members. Set technical direction, modernize legacy systems, and balance near-term business needs with long-term platform investments.
  • Make reliability a competitive advantage. Establish high standards for availability, performance, observability, security, and incident response. Build resilient systems that proactively detect and prevent failures, ensuring members can trust Life360 in the moments that matter most.
  • Build a culture of ownership and accountability. Create an engineering organization where teams proactively identify problems, take responsibility for outcomes, and drive solutions without waiting for direction. Empower leaders to make decisions, challenge the status quo, and continuously raise the bar for engineering excellence across organizational boundaries.
  • Make the invisible visible. Establish meaningful engineering metrics across reliability, performance, cost, security, and developer productivity. Use data to identify risks, prioritize investments, and communicate platform health and business impact to senior leadership.
  • Grow leaders who grow teams. Hire, coach, and develop engineering managers, staff engineers, and technical leaders. Build a high-performing organization with clear accountability, strong technical judgment, and leaders who can make decisions and deliver outcomes independently.
  • Accelerate the entire engineering organization. Build reusable services, APIs, and platforms that reduce duplication and enable product teams to ship faster. Expand our partner ecosystem through secure, scalable integrations that make it easier to build on Life360.
  • Turn engineering investments into business outcomes. Connect technical strategy to member experience, product velocity, and business performance. Make deliberate tradeoffs across reliability, scalability, cost, and speed, and use meaningful metrics to demonstrate impact and inform investment decisions.
  • Lead through influence. Partner across Product, Security, Data, and Engineering to align priorities, resolve ambiguity, and drive cross-functional decisions. Translate company strategy into actionable engineering roadmaps while bringing technical risks and tradeoffs to senior leadership.
  • Stay close to the technology and embrace what’s next. Engage in architectural reviews and critical technical decisions, challenge assumptions, and empower teams to make pragmatic tradeoffs. Champion AI-assisted development, automation, and modern engineering practices to improve productivity, quality, and speed.

What We’re Looking For

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience, including 5+ years leading engineering teams, with experience managing managers.
  • Track record of leading backend or platform engineering at high scale, with distributed systems serving millions of users. B2B or B2C platform experience is welcome.
  • Demonstrated success developing and coaching managers, including former individual contributors who grew into leadership.
  • Experience translating company strategy into technical plans, and representing your teams’ needs back to senior leaders.
  • Experience modernizing legacy systems with respect for the history behind them, and the judgment to change what needs changing rather than everything.
  • Strong cross-functional partnership skills, with a record of resolving ownership and priority conflicts directly.
  • Hands-on technical credibility in cloud infrastructure and distributed systems (AWS experience preferred).
  • Excellent written and verbal communication.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

Our Benefits

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.
  • 401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.
  • Paid parental leave.
  • Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being.
  • Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns.
  • Learning & Development programs.
  • Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment.
  • Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

Life360 Values

Our company’s mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference

  • Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust.
  • Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it’s hard.
  • Members Before Metrics - We focus on building an exceptional experience for families.
  • High Intensity, High Impact - We do whatever it takes to get the job done.

Our Commitment to Diversity

We believe that different ideas, perspectives and backgrounds create a stronger and more creative work environment that delivers better results. Together, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports, and celebrates the diverse voices of our employees. It fuels our innovation and connects us closer to our customers and the communities we serve. We strive to create a workplace that reflects the communities we serve and where everyone feels empowered to bring their authentic best selves to work.

Practice at the top of your license, from wherever you do your best work. This role is designed for psychiatrists who want meaningful clinical autonomy without having to build and operate a private practice alone.

We are looking for clinically excellent, patient-centered psychiatrists to provide psychiatric care through telehealth. Full-time and part-time positions are available.

jobs.excerpt: Bess/PV Engineer BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF SUNSTRONG MANAGEMENT SunStrong Management is a leading independent asset management and servicing platform specializing in residential and commercial solar energy portfolios.
jobs.description:
Bess/PV Engineer


BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF SUNSTRONG MANAGEMENT
SunStrong Management is a leading independent asset management and servicing platform specializing in residential and commercial solar energy portfolios. SunStrong provides end-to-end services including operations and maintenance, customer billing and support, asset performance management, and investor reporting. The company partners with leading capital providers to optimize clean energy assets at scale, supporting the growth of distributed renewable energy while delivering reliable performance and exceptional customer experience

POSITION OVERVIEW

The BESS/PV Engineer is the owner-side technical authority for SunStrong Management's solar PV and battery energy storage delivery portfolio. The role reviews designs, interrogates contractor engineering and test results, and establishes the technical position that Project Managers and gate decisions rest on, across SSM-originated, re-powering, remediation, and inherited in-flight projects, working with EPCs, OEMs, utilities, AHJs, and field service partners.
Project Delivery reports into Commercial Operations by design. The organization that will operate an asset for thirty years sets the standard by which it is accepted at twelve months. A project is not delivered when it is complete; it is delivered when Operations can run it.
The distinguishing expectation is independent technical judgment. The Engineer does not forward the EPC's engineering with a cover note. The Engineer recalculates the contractor's capacity test, finds the protection coordination gap before energization, and recognizes when a battery fire-safety submittal rests on test data that does not match the as-built configuration, and says so in writing.
The Engineer evaluates and recommends. The role does not direct the EPC's means and methods, approve change orders, or make gate decisions; those authorities sit with the Director and the gate owner per SSM-PD-001. Where the Engineer's technical position and a Project Manager's forecast disagree, both are reported and the gap is escalated to the Director.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Design Review & Engineering Standards

  • Lead the technical review of PV and BESS design packages — single-lines, array and block layouts, DC and AC collection, grounding, medium-voltage and protection design, controls architecture, and civil and structural interfaces — against the contracted scope and SSM standards.
  • Verify that design basis assumptions are conservative and traceable — module and inverter derates, DC/AC ratio, clipping, degradation, BESS usable energy, round-trip efficiency, auxiliary load, and availability — and that they match the assumptions behind the performance guarantees.
  • Review short-circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, and grounding studies; confirm that each study describes the equipment actually procured rather than a reference design.
  • Review BESS safety design — enclosure and block spacing, thermal management, fire detection and suppression, explosion control and ventilation, and emergency response planning — against NFPA 855, NEC Article 706, UL 9540 and UL 9540A test data, and AHJ requirements. Confirm that the test data applies to the configuration being installed.
  • Provide the technical content of the operability review of drawing sets against SSM standards — O&M access, equipment standardization against the fleet, monitoring and points architecture, protection and isolation, spares, and maintainability. Operability comments cost nothing at design review and cost a mobilization after energization.
  • Author and maintain the SSM fleet equipment standard, reference design details, and engineering review checklists in partnership with Portfolio Management and Field Service.

Owner’s Engineering & EPC Technical Oversight

  • Review submittals, RFIs, and engineering change requests; return technical dispositions with the reasoning stated, not only the outcome.
  • Define the technical content of Inspection and Test Plans — hold and witness points, acceptance criteria, and required records — for PV, BESS, and medium-voltage scopes; witness factory and site acceptance tests as assigned.
  • Evaluate nonconformances for technical significance and recommend disposition; distinguish a documentation defect from a defect in the installed work.
  • Evaluate the technical basis of change order requests — design deficiency, scope gap the contractor should have caught, or genuine added scope — and provide that evaluation to the Project Manager and Project Controls.
  • Review equipment selection and substitution requests against the SSM fleet standard, warranty terms, and long-term serviceability, including spares availability and OEM service coverage.
  • Reconcile as-built conditions to the design record; where drawings and field conditions disagree, the field condition governs the record and the drawings are corrected.
  • Support the as-is technical assessment of inherited in-flight construction — equipment condition, installed versus designed configuration, and surviving test records — to establish a defensible baseline.

Commissioning, Testing & Performance Validation

  • Review commissioning plans, procedures, and test protocols for inverters, PCS, battery systems, EMS and plant controller, protection, and SCADA before testing begins; recommend acceptance or return with comments.
  • Witness commissioning activities as assigned — inverter and PCS startup, BESS energization and first charge, protection relay testing, and utility witness testing.
  • Independently recalculate PV capacity and performance test results (for example, per ASTM E2848 where contracted) and BESS capacity, round-trip efficiency, ramp rate, response time, and availability results against the contracted test protocol rather than accepting the contractor’s computation.
  • Verify EMS and plant controller behavior — dispatch, state-of-charge limits, ramp and power-factor control, curtailment response, and applicable interconnection and ride-through requirements — against the interconnection agreement and offtake obligations.
  • Validate monitoring end to end with the Portfolio Manager — points-to-points against the SSM data model, alarm verification, and continuous clean data over the validation window.
  • Produce the post-completion performance analysis — measured PI, BESS capacity, and efficiency against expectation at 30, 90, and 180 days. A project is not closed when the work is finished; it is closed when the performance it was built to deliver has been demonstrated.

Performance Analysis, Failure Analysis & Remediation Engineering

  • Support re-powering and remediation scopes with technical scope definition — module, inverter, tracker, and BOS replacement; DC/AC rebalancing; BESS augmentation and retrofit — including the interconnection, structural, and protection implications that distinguish them from new construction.
  • Perform root cause analysis on equipment failures, underperformance, and recurring faults; distinguish defect, design deficiency, installation error, and operating condition, and document the basis to a standard that survives manufacturer and insurer review.
  • Provide the technical substantiation for warranty, performance guarantee, and insurance claims — failure evidence, test data, and loss quantification — in support of the Project Manager who owns the claim.
  • Analyze fleet performance data — production, availability, degradation, battery state of health, and alarm history — and route recurring failure modes into design standards and contractor and equipment selection.
  • Track product safety notices, recalls, code-cycle changes, and the field history of installed platforms; recommend the fleet response.

Safety & Compliance

  • Verify design and construction compliance with NEC, IEEE, UL, NFPA, AHJ, and utility requirements.
  • Support development and review of BESS emergency response plans, hazard mitigation analysis, and first-responder coordination.
  • Provide engineering input to JHAs, PEC/LOTO requirements, and energization sequencing, including stored-energy hazards in DC and battery systems.
  • Exercise stop-work authority without hesitation when design or installed conditions create an imminent hazard. SSM supports every exercise of stop-work authority by owner-side personnel without exception.
  • Support incident and near-miss investigation, including thermal events, with technical analysis independent of the party that performed the work.

Documentation & Technical Records

  • Maintain the technical record on assigned projects — design basis, review comments and dispositions, test records, and approved deviations — so that every position is traceable to evidence.
  • Verify the technical content of turnover documentation — as-builts, test records, firmware and configuration baselines, manuals, and warranty documentation — for completeness, legibility, and attribution; reject incomplete submissions rather than backfilling them.
  • Provide equipment serial numbers, firmware versions, and configuration baselines to the equipment register as construction data lands, so that delivery data reconciles to operations data after turnover.
  • Participate in lessons-learned reviews and route findings back into design standards and contractor selection.
QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering required; mechanical, power, or related engineering discipline considered with relevant experience.
  • Five or more years of solar PV and/or battery energy storage experience in design, owner’s engineering, commissioning, or performance engineering.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license preferred; EIT with a defined path to licensure considered.
  • Working command of PV and BESS system design — string and central inverter architectures, DC-coupled and AC-coupled storage, medium-voltage collection, and protection and controls.
  • Working knowledge of NEC Articles 690, 705, and 706; IEEE 1547 and 2800; NFPA 855; UL 9540 and 9540A; and utility interconnection requirements.
  • Ability to read and interrogate electrical single-lines, protection schemes, civil and structural drawings, and equipment specifications.
  • Direct experience with commissioning and capacity or performance testing of PV and BESS, including independent recalculation of test results.
  • Proficiency with PVsyst or equivalent, AutoCAD or Bluebeam, and familiarity with power-system study software (ETAP, SKM, or PowerFactory) sufficient to review studies. Data analysis in Excel, Python, or SQL preferred.
  • Experience with multiple BESS platforms and EMS or plant controller integration strongly preferred.
  • Experience with re-powering, remediation, or inherited in-flight construction preferred.
  • Demonstrated written precision. Technical positions produced by this role become the evidentiary basis for SSM warranty, claim, and acceptance positions.
  • OSHA 30 and NFPA 70E awareness current or obtainable within ninety days. NABCEP certification preferred.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to travel as needed

  • Comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and 401(k)

jobs.description:
Job Title: Product Manager & Designer

Status: Full-Time

Reports To: Head of Product

About Here Now Health:

Here Now Health is the first virtual healthcare company specifically built for children and families impacted by the child welfare system. We deliver child welfare–informed, high-touch care to Medicaid-covered youth navigating foster care, adoption, kinship placements, and juvenile justice. Our model prioritizes consistency, trust, and accessibility in systems where they are too often missing.

Role Summary

We are hiring the second person on our product team: someone who designs the screen, writes the ticket, chases the bug with the engineers, and sees it ship.

A therapist has ten minutes between sessions. A caregiver is reading a text in a parking lot. A caseworker needs to know what consent to sign. All three are looking at software we built, and the screen has to be right for each of them.

You own that screen: what it needs to do, how it looks, the ticket, the build, the check before it ships, and the release note after. Most days you are working directly with the engineers: reproducing what broke, showing them where and why, and working out the fix together. You report to the Head of Product and you are the second person on the product team.


Key Responsibilities

Roughly how the time splits

Working with engineering (about 40%)

  • Decide, with the Head of Product, which of the incoming bug reports and ideas ships next
  • Write the ticket for what you designed: states, error copy, notification text, what counts as done
  • Reproduce what breaks, show the engineers where and why, and brainstorm the fix with them
  • Check the build on staging with test patients, and look at production after a release
  • Write the release note, and run a short training when a feature changes how therapists work

Product design (about 30%)

  • Work out what therapists, care advocates (our non-clinical team who help families get scheduled and stay in care), caseworkers, and families each need from the same workflow, where those needs collide, and what has to be true for all of them before anything gets drawn
  • Take a workflow and a rough sketch to a low-fidelity screen the same week, and to a real one after a round with the clinical team
  • Own the copy across the product, from a reminder text to a button label, and the design system underneath it

Data and AI workflows (about 20%)

  • Keep our automated reports and checks accurate (attendance, therapist capacity, no-shows, chart audits), and follow up on what they surface
  • Build new AI-assisted workflows with the Head of Product, and check their output before anyone relies on it
  • Pull the numbers behind each product decision, and check after launch whether it worked
  • Turn a spreadsheet into something the team can act on, from monthly goals versus actuals to a quick answer for the clinical director

Materials and website (about 10%)

  • Build the decks and one-pagers the rest of the team needs: the monthly all-hands deck, a handout for a referral partner, materials for a conference
  • Keep the public-facing website current

Qualifications

Required

  • 3 to 5 years in product management, product design, or both, on a product people use every day
  • Healthcare experience, ideally Medicaid or behavioral health
  • A portfolio with product UI and at least one ticket or spec you wrote
  • A clear view of what makes a ticket and its acceptance criteria good
  • Figma or a similar tool, and the habit of writing your own UI copy
  • Daily use of AI tools in your own work, and a sense of where they go wrong
  • Enough technical depth to reproduce a bug, narrow it down, and explain it to an engineer. You don't need to code
  • Ability to pass a background check

Preferred

  • Child welfare or behavioral health experience
  • Experience on a product with several user roles and permissions
  • Experience managing work in Linear or a similar issue tracker
  • Experience building or maintaining a website in Webflow or a similar platform

Work Environment & Hours

  • 100% remote, with occasional travel for engagement with partners and stakeholders
  • Full-time role with flexible scheduling
  • Must have access to a private, quiet workspace with reliable high speed internet.

What Sets This Role Apart

  • What you design ships to therapists and families within weeks
  • You are in the room with the engineers every day. Bugs get chased together, often the same hour they are reported
  • Six kinds of users share one product, and each of them is right about what they need
  • Medicaid rules, consent law, and privacy decide a lot about what a screen can do. You design inside that
  • We use AI tools to support our workflows and expect you to be curious about them. The thinking and the creative work are still yours

We're a small team, so you'll do your own QA, copy, and prototypes, with engineers and clinicians a message away. Feedback often comes as a quick Slack note from a therapist between sessions, and you'll follow up with them to learn more.

Compensation and Benefits

Compensation

  • Salary: $90,000 - $100,000 annually based on experience

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance with 100% employer-paid employee-only premiums and significant contributions toward family coverage.
  • Company-sponsored 401(k) retirement plan.
  • Paid time off (PTO), paid sick leave, company holidays, and floating holidays.
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) for eligible high-deductible health plans.
  • Company-provided laptops and equipment, as applicable.
  • Reimbursement for approved business-related travel expenses.
  • Flexible and remote work arrangements

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification, scheduled hours, plan requirements, and applicable company policies.

About the Role

Join a data infrastructure and analytics team building a platform that turns information from many sources into reliable, current company intelligence. You will own the platform end to end, from architecture and ingestion through production operations, helping power downstream products with trusted data.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build a multi-source data platform for concurrent ingestion, event-driven processing, and orchestrated batch workflows.

  • Ingest data from provider APIs, webhooks, files, and web scraping, with rate limiting and robust failure handling.

  • Orchestrate scheduled workflows and historical backfills using tools such as Airflow, Dagster, or Prefect.

  • Build messaging and task queue workflows with retries, dead-letter queues, and controlled replay.

  • Preserve original payloads in Google Cloud Storage and transform data with dbt into raw, standardized, and curated layers.

  • Develop idempotent upserts, data contracts, automated quality checks, pipeline tests, and monitoring for freshness and failures.

  • Design and optimize PostgreSQL schemas and loading patterns for reliable downstream use.

  • Integrate data enrichment and LLM-based structured extraction into the platform.

What We're Looking For

  • 5 to 10 or more years of experience, including production ownership of multi-source data platforms from architecture through deployment and ongoing operation.

  • Strong hands-on experience with Airflow or similar orchestration tools, dbt, and Google Cloud Platform.

  • Experience building event-driven systems with messaging or task queues and asynchronous processing.

  • Strong SQL and PostgreSQL skills, including data modeling, query optimization, and incremental loading.

  • Proficiency in Python and concurrent or asynchronous processing, such as asyncio, aiohttp, or HTTPX.

  • Practical web scraping experience with tools such as Scrapy, Playwright, or Selenium.

  • Experience with data contracts, storage layers, and automated data quality checks. Entity resolution is valuable; BigQuery, Dataform, and LLM-based structured extraction are helpful.

  • Comfort working in a startup or small team with broad ownership and adaptability.

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology — setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own

  • Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

  • Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

  • Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

  • Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

  • Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

  • Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

  • Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

  • Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

  • Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

  • Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

  • Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

  • Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

  • Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

  • Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

  • Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

  • Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

  • Strong ownership mentality — when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For

  • Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

  • Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

  • Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

  • Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

  • People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

  • Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical / engineering leadership interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

The Analyst will help translate statutory, regulatory, program plan, technical, and operational requirements into clear guidance, tools, processes, and documentation assisting CAA to deliver harmonized services and support a cohesive implementation approach across states.

Working in a highly regulated and evolving environment, the Analyst will synthesize complex information for internal teams, producers, and other interest holders. jobs.title: Principal Consultant, Data 360 (Data Cloud)
jobs.excerpt: About Us - CloudMasonryCloudMasonry is a full-service Salesforce consultancy with multi-cloud expertise, serving enterprise clients through onshore, collaborative teams.
jobs.description:
About Us - CloudMasonry

CloudMasonry is a full-service Salesforce consultancy with multi-cloud expertise, serving enterprise clients through onshore, collaborative teams. Senior consultants shape the solution, and we were the first Salesforce consultancy to build AI into a complete delivery methodology, where it keeps requirements, documentation, and reporting moving so our teams spend more time with clients.
With offices in the US and UK, 65+ consultants holding 350+ Salesforce certifications, 559+ completed projects, a 4.9 CSAT, and an 89% repeat-client rate, CloudMasonry works with enterprise clients on their most complex Salesforce programs.

About the Role

The Principal Consultant, Data 360 is a hands-on, client-facing delivery role within CloudMasonry’s Data & AI Practice. You will design and build the data foundation our clients rely on: ingesting data from Salesforce and external systems, modeling it, resolving identities, and activating unified profiles and insights back into the applications and agents their teams use every day.

Your primary focus is Data 360, with the ability to also deliver on core Salesforce CRM. Data 360 work rarely lands on a clean org: unified profiles are built largely from Sales Cloud and Service Cloud data, activations are consumed back inside those clouds, and when a client asks why a record looks wrong, the answer is often in the CRM rather than the data platform. You will configure and troubleshoot Sales Cloud and Service Cloud yourself and advise on core object model and automation changes, and on blended engagements you may pick up CRM work directly.

This is a senior individual contributor position. You will own significant workstreams end to end, from requirements through configuration, testing, deployment, and client enablement. You will be the senior Data 360 voice on projects.

Success in this role means being comfortable with messy source data, unclear ownership, and clients who are still deciding what their data model should look like. You will bring an informed point of view, document decisions clearly, and diagnose root causes.

This role reports to the Data & AI Practice Lead and works closely with Solution Architects, Engagement Managers, and Project Leads on assigned engagements.

Key Responsibilities

Data 360 Implementation & Build

  • Configure data spaces, data streams, data lake and data model objects, transformations, and insights

  • Build ingestion pipelines from Salesforce and external systems into the Customer 360 model

  • Design and tune identity resolution rulesets, and validate unified profile output

  • Activate segments and insights to Marketing Cloud, core CRM, Agentforce, and other systems

Core Salesforce CRM

  • Configure and troubleshoot Sales Cloud and Service Cloud, including declarative automation

  • Advise on the core org changes Data 360 depends on, and take CRM workstreams when needed

Discovery & Design

  • Lead requirements and data discovery workshops with business and technical stakeholders

  • Produce source-to-target mappings, data models, identity resolution and functional designs

  • Advise on data governance, access control, consent handling, and consumption implications

  • Document data quality findings and recommend the permanent fix, not just a workaround

Client Delivery

  • Own delivery workstreams end-to-end in conjunction with a Project Manager: discovery, design, build, test, deploy, and hypercare

  • Communicate status, risks, and estimates, and raise risks early with the Engagement Manager

  • Run UAT and enable client admins to operate what we build

Ideal Candidate Profile

Experience

  • 5+ years of hands-on Salesforce experience, with at least 2 years implementing Data 360 (Data Cloud)

  • At least two full-lifecycle Data 360 implementations delivered in a client-facing or internal-customer-facing role, from discovery through production

  • Demonstrated ownership of identity resolution design on a real implementation

  • Consulting experience strongly preferred; systems integrator or agency background is a plus

  • Bachelor’s degree in a technical or business field, or equivalent applicable work experience

Data 360 Platform Expertise

  • Deep working knowledge of the Data 360 architecture: data spaces, data streams, data lake objects, data model objects, and the Customer 360 data model

  • Practical command of identity resolution: match rules, reconciliation rules, unified individual output, and how to debug a ruleset that is over- or under-matching

  • Segmentation, calculated insights, streaming insights, and activation targets including Marketing Cloud, core CRM, and Agentforce

  • Data transformations, both batch and streaming, and when each is appropriate

  • Data 360 connectors and ingestion patterns, including the Salesforce CRM connector, cloud storage, MuleSoft, and Ingestion API

  • Experience with zero-copy data sharing to and from Snowflake, Databricks, Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift, or other similar platforms

  • Strong SQL, including the ability to write and tune the queries behind calculated insights and transformations

  • Hands-on Sales Cloud and Service Cloud configuration experience, including object model design, permissions and sharing, and declarative automation (Flow, validation rules, permission sets)

  • Familiarity with Agentforce and how grounding an agent in Data 360 data works in practice is a plus

  • Experience with Tableau, Tableau Next, or CRM Analytics on top of Data 360 is a plus

  • Exposure to data migration and ETL tooling (MuleSoft, Informatica, Fivetran, dbt, or similar) is a plus

Delivery & Consulting Skills

  • Comfortable with the full range of project documentation, including business process documentation, requirements definition, configuration workbooks, data models, and detailed functional designs

  • Working fluency with Scrum or Agile delivery and with project management constructs such as RAID logs and RACI matrices

  • Sets and meets commitments, flags risk early, and proposes a mitigation rather than just the problem

  • Handles client disagreement directly and professionally, including telling a client when the thing they asked for is the wrong answer

  • High degree of self-management; able to run a workstream without daily direction

Communication

  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to write client-ready documents and lead workshops

  • Able to adjust register for the audience: technical depth with data engineers and admins, business framing with leaders

  • Explains data concepts in plain English without either oversimplifying or hiding behind jargon

  • Comfortable representing CloudMasonry in client and partner settings

Certifications

Required:

  • Salesforce Certified Administrator

  • Salesforce Certified Data 360 Consultant (formerly Data Cloud Consultant)

  • Salesforce Certified Sales Cloud Consultant or Service Cloud Consultant

Preferred:

  • Salesforce Certified Data Architect

  • Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist

  • Salesforce Certified Marketing Cloud Consultant or Email Specialist

  • Tableau or CRM Analytics credential

Other Requirements

  • Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities across multiple engagements

  • US-based and authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship

  • Travel requirements are contingent on client needs and may range from approximately 25% to 50%

Benefits & Perks

  • Full-time position with a competitive salary

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • 401(k) with up to a 4% company match

  • Unlimited PTO to maintain work-life balance

  • Parental leave for new parents

  • Paid company holidays

  • Salesforce certification reimbursement

  • Performance-based bonus eligibility

Diversity, Equity, & Inclusion

At CloudMasonry, diverse perspectives drive innovation. We embrace candidates from all backgrounds and experiences to build a stronger, more inclusive team. You will find your place with us if you are passionate about problem-solving and collaboration.

Application Process

After submitting your resume, you will receive an email invitation to complete an applicant assessment. This assessment helps us align your skills and attributes with the role. Candidates who do not complete the assessment will not be considered for the position.

Join CloudMasonry and take your Salesforce consulting career to the next level!

We participate in E-Verify, a federal program used to confirm employment eligibility and authorization to work in the United States.
